title: How to speak so that people want to listen
speaker: Julian Treasure

sentences.en: The human voice: It's the instrument we all play.
sentences.zh: 人声：这是我们大家演奏的乐器。

sentences.en: It's the most powerful sound in the world, probably.
sentences.zh: 这可能是世界上最有力的声音。

sentences.en: It's the only one that can start a war or say "I love you."
sentences.zh: 它是唯一一个可以发动战争或说“我爱你”的人。

sentences.en: And yet many people have the experience that when they speak, people don't listen to them.
sentences.zh: 然而，许多人都有这样的经历：当他们说话时，人们不听他们的。

sentences.en: And why is that? How can we speak powerfully to make change in the world?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么呢？我们怎样才能发出有力的声音来改变世界？

sentences.en: What I'd like to suggest, there are a number of habits that we need to move away from.
sentences.zh: 我想建议的是，我们需要改掉很多习惯。

sentences.en: I've assembled for your pleasure here seven deadly sins of speaking.
sentences.zh: 为了让您高兴，我在这里整理了七种言语的致命罪过。

sentences.en: I'm not pretending this is an exhaustive list, but these seven, I think, are pretty large habits that we can all fall into.
sentences.zh: 我并不是假装这是一个详尽的清单，但我认为这七个是我们所有人都可能陷入的相当大的习惯。

sentences.en: First, gossip. Speaking ill of somebody who's not present.
sentences.zh: 首先，八卦。说不在场的人的坏话。

sentences.en: Not a nice habit, and we know perfectly well the person gossiping, five minutes later, will be gossiping about us.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个好习惯，我们非常清楚那个八卦的人，五分钟后，就会八卦我们。

sentences.en: Second, judging. We know people who are like this in conversation, and it's very hard to listen to somebody if you know that you're being judged and found wanting at the same time.
sentences.zh: 第二，判断。我们知道有人在谈话中是这样的，如果你知道自己在被评判的同时又被认为有缺陷，那么你就很难倾听别人的意见。

sentences.en: Third, negativity. You can fall into this.
sentences.zh: 第三，消极情绪。你可能会陷入这样的境地。

sentences.en: My mother, in the last years of her life, became very negative, and it's hard to listen.
sentences.zh: 我的母亲在她生命的最后几年变得非常消极，很难倾听。

sentences.en: I remember one day, I said to her, "It's October 1 today," and she said, "I know, isn't it dreadful?"
sentences.zh: 记得有一天，我对她说：“今天是10月1日。”她说：“我知道，这不是很可怕吗？”

sentences.en: (Laughter) It's hard to listen when somebody's that negative.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 当有人那么消极时，很难去倾听。

sentences.en: (Laughter) And another form of negativity, complaining.
sentences.zh: （笑声）还有另一种形式的消极情绪，抱怨。

sentences.en: Well, this is the national art of the U.K.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是英国的民族艺术。

sentences.en: It's our national sport. We complain about the weather, sport, about politics, about everything, but actually, complaining is viral misery.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的国民运动。我们抱怨天气、体育、政治、一切，但实际上，抱怨是病毒式的痛苦。

sentences.en: It's not spreading sunshine and lightness in the world.
sentences.zh: 它并没有在世界上传播阳光和光明。

sentences.en: Excuses. We've all met this guy. Maybe we've all been this guy.
sentences.zh: 借口。我们都见过这个人。也许我们都曾经是这样的人。

sentences.en: Some people have a blamethrower. They just pass it on to everybody else and don't take responsibility for their actions, and again, hard to listen to somebody who is being like that.
sentences.zh: 有些人有一个指责者。他们只是将其传递给其他人，而不为自己的行为承担责任，而且，很难倾听这样的人的意见。

sentences.en: Penultimate, the sixth of the seven, embroidery, exaggeration.
sentences.zh: 倒数第二个，七个中的第六个，刺绣，夸张。

sentences.en: It demeans our language, actually, sometimes.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有时它贬低了我们的语言。

sentences.en: For example, if I see something that really is awesome, what do I call it?
sentences.zh: 例如，如果我看到一些非常棒的东西，我该怎么称呼它？

sentences.en: (Laughter) And then, of course, this exaggeration becomes lying, and we don't want to listen to people we know are lying to us.
sentences.zh: （笑声）然后，当然，这种夸张就变成了谎言，我们不想听那些我们知道对我们撒谎的人。

sentences.en: And finally, dogmatism. The confusion of facts with opinions.
sentences.zh: 最后 教条主义 混淆事实和观点

sentences.en: When those two things get conflated, you're listening into the wind.
sentences.zh: 当这两件事被混为一谈时 你就会听到风声

sentences.en: You know, somebody is bombarding you with their opinions as if they were true.
sentences.zh: 你知道,有人用他们的观点来攻击你 仿佛他们是真实的。

sentences.en: It's difficult to listen to that. So here they are, seven deadly sins of speaking.
sentences.zh: 很难听,所以他们在这里 说七种致命的罪

sentences.en: These are things I think we need to avoid.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我认为我们需要避免的事情。

sentences.en: But is there a positive way to think about this?
sentences.zh: 但是,是否有积极的方法来考虑这个问题?

sentences.en: Yes, there is. I'd like to suggest that there are four really powerful cornerstones, foundations, that we can stand on if we want our speech to be powerful and to make change in the world.
sentences.zh: 是的,有。我想建议,有四个非常强大的基石,基金会, 如果我们想要我们的演讲 强大和改变世界,我们就可以坚持下去。

sentences.en: Fortunately, these things spell a word. The word is "hail," and it has a great definition as well.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是,这些东西拼写了一个词。这个词是“万福”,它也有一个伟大的定义。

sentences.en: I'm not talking about the stuff that falls from the sky and hits you on the head.
sentences.zh: 我不是说从天上掉下来的 击中你的头的东西

sentences.en: I'm talking about this definition, to greet or acclaim enthusiastically, which is how I think our words will be received if we stand on these four things.
sentences.zh: 我说的是这个定义,欢迎或赞美, 我认为如果我们站在这四件事上, 我们的话就会被接受。

sentences.en: So what do they stand for? See if you can guess.
sentences.zh: 他们代表什么?

sentences.en: The H, honesty, of course, being true in what you say, being straight and clear.
sentences.zh: H,诚实,当然, 在你说的,是真实的, 直和清楚。

sentences.en: The A is authenticity, just being yourself.
sentences.zh: A是真实的,只是做你自己。

sentences.en: A friend of mine described it as standing in your own truth, which I think is a lovely way to put it.
sentences.zh: 我的一个朋友把它描述成 站在你自己的真理, 我认为这是一个可爱的方式 说它。

sentences.en: The I is integrity, being your word, actually doing what you say, and being somebody people can trust.
sentences.zh: 我是正直的, 作为你的诺言, 实际上做你所说的, 和某人可以信任。

sentences.en: And the L is love. I don't mean romantic love, but I do mean wishing people well, for two reasons.
sentences.zh: L是爱,我的意思不是浪漫的爱, 但我的意思是希望人们好,有两个原因。

sentences.en: First of all, I think absolute honesty may not be what we want.
sentences.zh: 首先,我认为绝对诚实可能不是我们想要的。

sentences.en: I mean, my goodness, you look ugly this morning.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是,我的天啊, 你今天早上看起来丑陋。

sentences.en: Perhaps that's not necessary. Tempered with love, of course, honesty is a great thing.
sentences.zh: 也许没必要 诚心爱是件好事

sentences.en: But also, if you're really wishing somebody well, it's very hard to judge them at the same time.
sentences.zh: 而且,如果你真的希望有人好, 很难同时判断他们。

sentences.en: I'm not even sure you can do those two things simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不确定你能同时做这两件事

sentences.en: So hail. Also, now that's what you say, and it's like the old song, it is what you say, it's also the way that you say it.
sentences.zh: 冰雹,你也是这么说的,就像老歌,你也是这么说的。

sentences.en: You have an amazing toolbox. This instrument is incredible, and yet this is a toolbox that very few people have ever opened.
sentences.zh: 你有一个惊人的工具箱。这个工具箱是令人难以置信的, 但是这是一个工具箱, 很少有人打开过。

sentences.en: I'd like to have a little rummage in there with you now and just pull a few tools out that you might like to take away and play with, which will increase the power of your speaking.
sentences.zh: 我现在想和你谈谈 拿出一些工具来玩 这会增加你说话的能量

sentences.en: Register, for example. Now, falsetto register may not be very useful most of the time, but there's a register in between.
sentences.zh: 比如说注册。现在,错误的注册在大部分时间里可能不是非常有用的, 但是在两者之间有一个注册。

sentences.en: I'm not going to get very technical about this for any of you who are voice coaches.
sentences.zh: 我对你们这些语音导音员来说 不太懂技术

sentences.en: You can locate your voice, however. So if I talk up here in my nose, you can hear the difference.
sentences.zh: 你可以找到自己的声音 如果我在鼻子里说话,你就能听到不同的声音

sentences.en: If I go down here in my throat, which is where most of us speak from most of the time.
sentences.zh: 如果我从喉咙里下去 大部分时间我们都是在这里说话的

sentences.en: But if you want weight, you need to go down here to the chest.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想要重量,你需要 下到这里的胸口。

sentences.en: You hear the difference? We vote for politicians with lower voices, it's true, because we associate depth with power and with authority.
sentences.zh: 你听到不同之处了吗?我们投票给声音低的政客,这是真的, 因为我们把深度与权力和权威联系在一起。

sentences.en: That's register. Then we have timbre. It's the way your voice feels.
sentences.zh: 那是登记表,然后我们有小便,这是你声音的感觉

sentences.en: Again, the research shows that we prefer voices which are rich, smooth, warm, like hot chocolate.
sentences.zh: 研究再次表明,我们更喜欢 富有、光滑、温暖的声音,像热巧克力。

sentences.en: Well if that's not you, that's not the end of the world, because you can train.
sentences.zh: 如果不是你,那也不是世界末日 因为你可以训练

sentences.en: Go and get a voice coach. And there are amazing things you can do with breathing, with posture, and with exercises to improve the timbre of your voice.
sentences.zh: 去找一个声音导师 呼吸、姿势和锻炼 都可以做一些了不起的事

sentences.en: Then prosody. I love prosody. This is the sing-song, the meta-language that we use in order to impart meaning.
sentences.zh: 然后装模作样。我喜欢装模作样。这是唱歌声,我们用来表达意义。

sentences.en: It's root one for meaning in conversation.
sentences.zh: 这是根一 意义在谈话。

sentences.en: People who speak all on one note are really quite hard to listen to if they don't have any prosody at all.
sentences.zh: 讲一个字的人真的很难听 如果他们没有 任何摆弄。

sentences.en: That's where the word "monotonic" comes from, or monotonous, monotone.
sentences.zh: 这就是"调子"这个词的来源 或单调的单调

sentences.en: Also, we have repetitive prosody now coming in, where every sentence ends as if it were a question when it's actually not a question, it's a statement?
sentences.zh: 而且,我们有 重复的摆弄,现在进来, 每一个句子结束 似乎这是一个问题 当它实际上不是一个问题, 这是一个声明?

sentences.en: (Laughter) And if you repeat that one, it's actually restricting your ability to communicate through prosody, which I think is a shame, so let's try and break that habit.
sentences.zh: 如果你再说一遍, 它实际上是限制你的能力 沟通 通过假肢, 我认为这是一个耻辱, 所以让我们尝试打破习惯。

sentences.en: Pace. I can get very excited by saying something really quickly, or I can slow right down to emphasize, and at the end of that, of course, is our old friend silence.
sentences.zh: 我可以很快地说点什么来让我很兴奋, 或者我也可以慢慢来强调, 在那之后,当然,我们老朋友的沉默。

sentences.en: There's nothing wrong with a bit of silence in a talk, is there?
sentences.zh: 在谈话中沉默一点没什么不对的,是吗?

sentences.en: We don't have to fill it with ums and ahs.
sentences.zh: 我们不用用Ums和Ahs填满它

sentences.en: It can be very powerful. Of course, pitch often goes along with pace to indicate arousal, but you can do it just with pitch.
sentences.zh: 它可能非常强大。当然,投球通常与速度相配合,以显示振奋,但只要投球就可以做到。

sentences.en: Where did you leave my keys? (Higher pitch) Where did you leave my keys?
sentences.zh: 你把我的钥匙放哪儿了?

sentences.en: So, slightly different meaning in those two deliveries.
sentences.zh: 所以,在这两批货物中,含义略有不同。

sentences.en: And finally, volume. (Loud) I can get really excited by using volume.
sentences.zh: 最后,音量。 (Loud)我可以用音量来感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Sorry about that, if I startled anybody.
sentences.zh: 对不起,如果我吓到任何人。

sentences.en: Or, I can have you really pay attention by getting very quiet.
sentences.zh: 或者,我可以让你 真正关注 通过得到非常安静。

sentences.en: Some people broadcast the whole time. Try not to do that.
sentences.zh: 有些人一直都在广播,别那么做

sentences.en: That's called sodcasting, (Laughter) Imposing your sound on people around you carelessly and inconsiderately.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的 sodcasting，（笑声）把你的声音不经意地、不经意地强加给你周围的人。

sentences.en: Not nice. Of course, where this all comes into play most of all is when you've got something really important to do.
sentences.zh: 不太好。当然，这一切最重要的是当你有一些非常重要的事情要做时。

sentences.en: It might be standing on a stage like this and giving a talk to people.
sentences.zh: 它可能会站在这样的舞台上向人们演讲。

sentences.en: It might be proposing marriage, asking for a raise, a wedding speech.
sentences.zh: 可能是求婚、要求加薪、婚礼致辞。

sentences.en: Whatever it is, if it's really important, you owe it to yourself to look at this toolbox and the engine that it's going to work on, and no engine works well without being warmed up.
sentences.zh: 不管它是什么，如果它真的很重要，你就应该看看这个工具箱和它将要工作的引擎，没有引擎在没有预热的情况下可以很好地工作。

sentences.en: Warm up your voice. Actually, let me show you how to do that.
sentences.zh: 温暖你的声音。实际上，让我向您展示如何做到这一点。

sentences.en: Would you all like to stand up for a moment?
sentences.zh: 大家愿意站起来一会儿吗？

sentences.en: I'm going to show you the six vocal warm-up exercises that I do before every talk I ever do.
sentences.zh: 我将向您展示我在每次演讲之前都会做的六个声音热身练习。

sentences.en: Any time you're going to talk to anybody important, do these.
sentences.zh: 每当你要与重要的人交谈时，请执行以下操作。

sentences.en: First, arms up, deep breath in, and sigh out, ahhhhh, like that.
sentences.zh: 首先，双臂举起，深吸一口气，然后呼出，啊啊啊，就这样。

sentences.en: One more time. Ahhhh, very good. Now we're going to warm up our lips, and we're going to go Ba, Ba. Very good.
sentences.zh: 再一次。啊啊啊，非常好。现在我们要预热我们的嘴唇，然后我们要“Ba，Ba”。非常好。

sentences.en: And now, brrrrrrrrrr, just like when you were a kid.
sentences.zh: 现在，brrrrrrrrrrr，就像你小时候一样。

sentences.en: Brrrr. Now your lips should be coming alive.
sentences.zh: 呜呜。现在你的嘴唇应该活跃起来了。

sentences.en: We're going to do the tongue next with exaggerated la, la.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们要用夸张的“啦，啦”来练习舌头。

sentences.en: Beautiful. You're getting really good at this.
sentences.zh: 美丽的。你在这方面已经做得非常好了。

sentences.en: And then, roll an R. Rrrrrrr. That's like champagne for the tongue.
sentences.zh: 然后，掷 R。Rrrrrrr。这就像舌头上的香槟。

sentences.en: Finally, and if I can only do one, the pros call this the siren.
sentences.zh: 最后，如果我只能做一件事，专业人士称之为警报。

sentences.en: It's really good. It starts with "we" and goes to "aw."
sentences.zh: 真的很好。它以“我们”开头，然后到“哦”。

sentences.en: The "we" is high, the "aw" is low. So you go, weeeaawww, weeeaawww.
sentences.zh: “我们”高，“aw”低。所以你走吧，weeeaawww，weeeaawww。

sentences.en: Fantastic. Give yourselves a round of applause.
sentences.zh: 极好的。给自己热烈的掌声。

sentences.en: Take a seat, thank you. (Applause) Next time you speak, do those in advance.
sentences.zh: 请坐，谢谢。 （鼓掌）下次讲话的时候，提前做好这些。

sentences.en: Now let me just put this in context to close.
sentences.zh: 现在让我把这个放在上下文中结束。

sentences.en: This is a serious point here. This is where we are now, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一个严肃的问题。这就是我们现在所处的位置，对吗？

sentences.en: We speak not very well to people who simply aren't listening in an environment that's all about noise and bad acoustics.
sentences.zh: 我们对那些在充满噪音和糟糕音响效果的环境中根本不听话的人说话不太好。

sentences.en: I have talked about that on this stage in different phases.
sentences.zh: 我在这个舞台上分不同阶段讲过这个问题。

sentences.en: What would the world be like if we were speaking powerfully to people who were listening consciously in environments which were actually fit for purpose?
sentences.zh: 如果我们对那些在真正适合目的的环境中有意识地倾听的人进行强有力的讲话，世界会是什么样子？

sentences.en: Or to make that a bit larger, what would the world be like if we were creating sound consciously and consuming sound consciously and designing all our environments consciously for sound?
sentences.zh: 或者说得更大一点，如果我们有意识地创造声音、有意识地消费声音、有意识地为声音设计我们所有的环境，世界会是什么样子？

sentences.en: That would be a world that does sound beautiful, and one where understanding would be the norm, and that is an idea worth spreading.
sentences.zh: 那将是一个听起来确实很美丽的世界，一个理解将成为常态的世界，这是一个值得传播的想法。

sentences.en: Thank you. (Applause)
sentences.zh: 谢谢。 （掌声）
